NEW DELHI: Indian authorities removed queue liners outside the Pakistan high commission visa section along with other encroachment on a lane outside the boundary of the compound. The action Wednesday followed removal of parking poles and security barricades outside the Indian high commission in Islamabad earlier this week.Official sources said the liners were removed from a side lane outside the high commission and not the main gate. The response was said to be proportionate to the Pakistani action outside the Indian mission. Official sources said India was hoping the matter would end here but added govt would respond accordingly if Pakistan chooses to escalate.India’s ties with Pakistan remain in a freeze with govt last year — after the Pahalgam terror attack — cutting down the strength of high commissions from the already downgraded 55 to 30. Both sides continue to have functional engagements though, including DGMO-level talks, exchange of pre-notification of flight testing of ballistic missiles, exchange of list of nuclear installations, and exchange of list of prisoners in each other’s custody.India strongly denies having any Track-2 dialogue with Pakistan.Visuals showed that India’s action left a trail of rubble outside the mission, with broken metal railings and gates, twisted metal frames, roofing sheets, bricks and chunks of concrete and plaster strewn across the paved area. The main entrance of the high commission, with its white walls, domed features and large metal gates bearing the Pakistani emblem, remained intact.
Article Summary: India removed queue liners outside the pakistan high commission visa section along with other encroachment on a lane outside the boundary of the compound. Official sources said india was hoping the matter would end here but added govt would respond accordingly if pakistan chooses to escalate.

Article Title: Centre, UT govt have made J&K safer, says US envoy
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: In a rare public affirmation of India's sovereignty over J&K by a top US diplomat, ambassador Sergio Gor said Wednesday the UT is an important part of India and said Washington will consider downgrading its highest "do not travel" warning for J&K.Gor made the remarks in a joint briefing with J&K CM Omar Abdullah in Srinagar, during what's the first standalone visit by a US envoy to the UT after abrogation of Art 370 in 2019. His remarks are seen by Indian officials as validating India's sovereignty and territorial integrity, and post-2018 counterterror strategy and governance reforms. Later, Pakistan summoned the US Charge d'Affaires in Islamabad and lodged a demarche.Pakistan summoned the US Charge d’Affaires in Islamabad to lodge a “strong protest” over what it described as factually incorrect, referring to remarks by Gor on the status of J&K. Pakistan also claimed Gor’s “irresponsible” statement negated the long-standing position of US on J&K.“US puts out travel warnings and every so often, we re-evaluate those travel warnings. I cannot make any big announcements here today, but it is something we are going to look at,” said Gor who will visit Ladakh Thursday.“New Delhi, the chief minister here, the govt here, we believe have made some incredible steps to keeping this area safer and making it more safe,” added Gor.In remarks that could signal to other western countries to re-evaluate their own travel advisories, Gor said a lot of Americans would “enjoy coming here and seeing the beauty and the opportunities that exist here”.“So, we will be looking at if the travel warning that is imposed and recommended by US is something that should be downgraded because, as I said earlier, this is a beautiful area,” he said.US State Department currently maintains Level-4 travel warning for J&K. To downgrade the advisory, according to American authorities, US verifies sustained reductions in terror incidents, long-term political stability, ease of movement for foreign nationals, and reliable emergency consular access. Gor called on Abdullah at his residence soon after reaching Srinagar.“I am thrilled to be here. We just had a very good meeting and we have some follow-ups that we hope to take back to Washington (and) back to Delhi. But a very warm, a very cordial meeting and we look forward to building this relationship forward,” he said.Abdullah said he discussed with Gor the relations between Delhi and Washington with a specific focus on J&K. “It was a very good meeting. We had an opportunity to discuss the relations between our two countries, but with a specific focus on what US can do with J&K,” the CM said.“There are obviously certain legacy issues that over time we will be working to resolve. But we look forward to taking this conversation further...” Abdullah said.
Article Summary: Us state department currently maintains level-4 travel warning for j&k. Pakistan summoned the us charge d’affaires in islamabad to lodge a “strong protest” over what it described as factually incorrect. Pakistan also claimed gor’s “irresponsible” statement negated the long-standing position of us on j &k.

NEW DELHI: The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) has urged the US government to impose sanctions on members of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), rather than honouring them with “high-level meetings. ”The statement from the USCIRF comes ahead of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat ’s scheduled visit to the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, beginning August 25.In a post on X, the commission shared remarks from Asif Mahmood, a Pakistani-American physician who serves as its chair, and Commissioner Gene Mills.Mahmood described the RSS, the ideological parent of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), as an umbrella organisation, alleging that its affiliated groups had carried out attacks on religious minorities.Mills, meanwhile, said RSS leaders, even when affiliated with the Indian government, should not be given high-level meetings or diplomatic courtesies. Instead, he urged Washington to focus on imposing sanctions on RSS members found responsible for violations of freedom of religion or belief.The latest comments follow USCIRF's annual report released in March, in which the commission criticised India over alleged religious freedom violations and backed “targeted sanctions” against individuals and entities, including the RSS and the Research and Analysis Wing (RAW), India's external intelligence agency.New Delhi firmly rejected the report, accusing the watchdog of presenting a “distorted and selective” picture of the country based on “questionable sources and ideological narratives.”USCIRF is a US federal government agency, but its role is purely advisory and its recommendations are non-binding.Bhagwat, meanwhile, is scheduled to undertake the three-nation visit at the invitation of various local associations and organisations associated with the Indian diaspora. The visit comes as the RSS marks its centenary year. During his trip, he is expected to interact with members of the Indian diaspora and representatives of local organisations.
Article Summary: Mohan bhagwat will be on a three-nation tour from august 25. During his trip, he is expected to interact with members of the indian diaspora. NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra on Thursday penned emotional notes for their mother Sonia Gandhi , who is set to release her memoir 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' in November.The messages came on the birth anniversary of their father, former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi, with both Rahul and Priyanka reflecting the relationship of their parents and the personal losses Sonia Gandhi endured over the years.Rahul, addressing his mother as 'Mama', recalled the last time he saw his parents together more than 35 years ago and spoke about Sonia Gandhi’s life after Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination in 1991."Mama, I last saw you and Papa together more than 35 years ago. Since the day Papa left, I have watched you face everything life threw at you with never-ending courage and dignity," Rahul wrote on X."Only Priyanka and I really know what you have been through, and how difficult your life after Papa truly was," he added.Rahul said he was proud that Sonia Gandhi, who has largely kept her personal life away from public view, had decided to tell her story."I am happy, and so proud, that your story 'Belonging: A Journey of Love' — will finally be read by the millions of people who love you. I know how hard it was for someone as private as you to tell the world your beautiful story," he wrote.Referring to Rajiv Gandhi’s birth anniversary, Rahul ended the note saying, "Today, on his birthday, I can see Papa smiling and looking down proudly at his beautiful Sonia."Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also shared a personal message, describing her parents’ relationship as "one of the greatest love stories of our time"."On my father’s birthday today, I think he would have been especially proud of my mother for having written her story with so much heart and honesty," she wrote.Priyanka said she felt privileged to have witnessed their relationship and hoped the memoir would allow readers to know Sonia Gandhi beyond her political persona."For me, it’s one of the greatest love stories of our time. I feel privileged to have witnessed it and I am happy that through her book, everyone will get to know my mother for what she truly is — a brave, loyal, compassionate woman, who is also tough as nails and great fun when she wants to be," she said.She described Sonia Gandhi as "a woman whose life has been a testament to her love for her husband and her country", before signing off: "Love you, ma and so, so proud of you."Sonia Gandhi’s memoir to release in NovemberPublisher Alfred A. Knopf announced earlier this week that Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love', will be published on November 10.The memoir traces her journey from her childhood in post-war Italy and her romance with Rajiv Gandhi during their time in Cambridge to her life in India and the personal tragedies that subsequently reshaped her life.Sonia Gandhi, 79, who remains the Congress’s longest-serving president, is also expected to revisit the assassinations of her mother-in-law and former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and her husband Rajiv Gandhi.The book’s cover features a black-and-white photograph of Sonia Gandhi from her youth.Describing the memoir, the publisher said it tells a story of "love, family, and an endlessly fascinating country: India", adding that the "once famously reticent Sonia Gandhi opens up with warmth and candor" about her life.Born in Italy, Sonia Gandhi was a 19-year-old student in Cambridge when she met Rajiv Gandhi in 1965. The couple married on February 25, 1968.The memoir is scheduled to be released on November 10, 2026.
Article Summary: Sonia gandhi's memoir is scheduled to be released on november 10. Leader of opposition rahul gandhi and congress mp priyanka gandhi vadra penned emotional notes for their mother. The messages came on the birth anniversary of their father, former prime minister rajiv gandhi. The memoir is scheduled to be released on november 10, 2026.

Article Title: 'UGC regulation under reconsideration', govt tells SC on controversial equity rules
Article Text:
The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the Supreme Court on January 29.

SC had earlier put regulations on hold

Court questioned provisions on caste discrimination

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday informed the Supreme Court that the 2026 University Grants Commission (UGC) equity regulations, which seek to address caste-based discrimination in higher education institutions, are currently being reconsidered.The development came during a hearing before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. The court was hearing several petitions challenging the validity of the regulations."This is the UGC regulation matter. It is under reconsideration," Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the bench.The Supreme Court subsequently directed the UGC to submit a comprehensive counter affidavit within four weeks. The petitioners will have two weeks after that to file their rejoinders, if any.The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the top court on January 29. At the time, the court said the provisions were "prima facie vague" and could have "very sweeping consequences", warning that they could potentially divide society and have a "dangerous impact".The court had also asked the Centre and the UGC to respond to three petitions challenging the new framework."In exercise of our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, we further direct that the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2012, will continue to operate and remain in force till further orders," it had said.The regulations had faced opposition in several places, with student groups and other organisations calling for their immediate withdrawal.While examining the regulations, the Supreme Court raised questions about how some of their provisions were framed.One concern related to Regulation 3(1)(c), which separately defines "caste-based discrimination". The court questioned why a separate definition was necessary when Regulation 3(1)(e) already contains a broader definition of "discrimination".The bench also questioned the exclusion of ragging from the regulations, noting that it remains a common form of harassment in educational institutions.The court had further observed that the wording of the 2026 regulations appeared "prima facie vague" and "capable of misuse".Advocate Vishnu Shankar Jain, representing one of the petitioners, had challenged Regulation 3(1)(c). The provision defines caste-based discrimination as discrimination "only on the basis of caste or tribe" against members of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes.
Article Summary: The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the supreme court on january 29. The court was hearing several petitions challenging the validity of the regulations. The regulations had faced opposition in several places, with student groups and other organisations calling for their immediate withdrawal.

Article Title: 'RSS believes it knows the truth for everyone': Rahul Gandhi attacks Sangh over ideology
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi's idea of 'Swaraj.

‘My Experiments with Truth’ reflects individual journeys

Rahul targets BJP-RSS over 'exclusion'

'Gandhi’s Swaraj is more than freedom'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha leader of opposition (LoP) Rahul Gandhi Thursday accused the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of trying to impose its idea of truth on people across India, arguing that every individual must have the freedom to find and define their own truth.Speaking at the "Hara Bhara Swaraj : A Tribute to Rajiv Gandhi 's Vision" programme in New Delhi, the Gandhi Scion described the ideological contest in India as a deeper struggle over how people understand themselves, freedom and their place in society.The Congress leader also drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi 's idea of 'Swaraj', saying no organisation or individual could claim to know what is true for another person."What Gandhiji was saying was that every living being is a unique entity with their own path towards the truth. I cannot tell you what your truth is. Today, the ideological battle in India is precisely that. It is not fundamentally about environment, politics, or free media--those are symptoms. The real fight is that a small group of people have decided, because they control the system, that they know the truth of everyone in this country.That is my problem with the RSS: the RSS has decided that they know the truth of 1.5 billion people. And I say, no. Only 1.5 billion people can know their own truth," Rahul Gandhi asserted.He said even he could not claim to understand another person's truth because people's experiences, families and circumstances are different."And I say, no. Only 1.5 billion people can know their own truth. Even I cannot do that. If I begin to believe that I know your truth, I would be a madman. Because I am not you. I haven't faced what you've faced; I haven't seen what you've seen; I haven't dealt with what you've dealt with. I don't have the same parents, the same friends, or the same life. So how can I say that I know your truth?" he added.Rahul Gandhi then referred to Mahatma Gandhi's autobiography, 'My Experiments with Truth', saying its title itself reflected the idea that truth is something each person explores through their own life."Please notice, Gandhiji's book was not called 'The Truth' or 'My Understanding of the Truth'. It was titled 'My Experiments with Truth'. I have experiments with my truth; you have experiments with your truth."The Congress leader also criticised the BJP and RSS over what he described as the exclusion of sections of Indian society. He said people from different religious and social communities must feel that they have an equal place in the country."Imagine what the BJP and RSS have done. Imagine if I walked into this room and told 15-17 per cent of you--Muslims, Christians, Sikhs--'You do not exist, and if you speak up, see what happens to you.' Then telling 10 per cent Adivasis, 'We will take your land whenever we want, and if you resist, we will shoot you,' and Dalits, 'You are complaining for nothing; everything is fine with the caste system.' That is what is being done to our motherland. Every single person in this country--regardless of religion, community, or gender--must feel: 'I belong here. I can walk freely in this country. I am loved, respected, and appreciated here, and my search for truth matters to the nation,'" he said.Rahul Gandhi also explained why he believes 'Swaraj' should not simply be understood as the same thing as freedom or liberty in the Western sense.He used US President Donald Trump and Mahatma Gandhi to illustrate the difference, arguing that being legally free does not necessarily mean having control over one's own actions and desires."'Swaraj' is often confused with the Western word 'freedom.' People think that Swaraj means freedom; that it means liberty or independence. No--Swaraj means rule over oneself (Swa par raj / self-governance). If you go to America and ask, 'Is Trump a free man?', everyone will say, 'Absolutely.' But if you ask, 'Does Trump rule over himself?', the clear answer is, 'No, he does not.' Whereas Gandhiji in a prison 80 years ago would say, 'I am not free, but I rule over myself. It is Swaraj,'" he explained.The Congress leader said this understanding of Swaraj makes it a personal responsibility rather than something that can simply be granted by a government or another person."Swaraj is an Indian concept, and it carries deep responsibility. It is a way of thinking, and it is an individual project. I cannot give you Swaraj. Whatever I do... in a Western sense, I can grant you freedom by saying, 'You are not in prison; I have given you freedom.'But I cannot give you Swaraj. Because Swaraj is your personal relationship with the universe. Swaraj is an individual path. And Gandhiji's conception of Swaraj was that every single person in this country should walk on this path. "His remarks placed the idea of individual self-rule at the centre of his criticism of the RSS, while presenting Gandhi's philosophy of Swaraj as one based on personal responsibility and the freedom of each individual to pursue their own understanding of truth.
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi says every individual must have the freedom to find and define their own truth. Congress leader also drew a distinction between the rss's worldview and mahatma gandhi's idea of 'swaraj' gandhi criticised the bjp and rss over what he described as the exclusion of sections of indian society.

SRINAGAR: A day after meeting Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah in Srinagar, US Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, arrived in Ladakh Thursday on his maiden visit to the Union Territory, where he went sightseeing and rafting. There were also reports that he was likely to meet the Dalai Lama, who is currently in Ladakh, during his two-day trip, but there was no confirmation about this from anyone.Shortly after landing, Gor went sightseeing in Leh and later participated in river rafting, covering several kilometres from Tsogti to Sangam, the confluence of Indus and Zanskar rivers.Officials said the US envoy’s team had approached for a meeting with Ladakh Lt-governor Vinai Kumar Saxena, but he was in New Delhi.They also said they had no idea whether Gor was meeting the Dalai Lama on Friday morning. The 91-year-old Tibetan spiritual leader has been recuperating in Ladakh since June 28 following a medical procedure on his left knee in New Delhi.This is the first visit by a top US diplomat to Ladakh since it was carved out as a UT from the former state of J&K in Aug 2019, and the Galwan clash between Indian and Chinese troops in June 2020 that led to a prolonged military standoff between the two countries in the region.Gor is also US President Donald Trump’s special envoy for South and Central Asia, and his visit to the two UTs bordering China and Pakistan is being seen as a message to the two countries.In Srinagar, Gor’s remark describing Kashmir as an important part of India drew a sharp reaction from Pakistan, which summoned the US embassy’s charge d’affaires in Islamabad and lodged a “strong demarche” over what it termed a “factually incorrect statement”.He also talked of US considering reviewing its security advisory for J&K.Asked about Pakistan’s reaction to Gor’s remarks, the J&K CM Thursday said: “This is a matter between Pakistan and America. Neither you nor I can do anything about it.”On Congress’s criticism that there was no need to hear from the US that Kashmir was an important part of India, Omar said, “They have a point of view and they are entitled to it. I am not going to get into a war of words over this.”
Article Summary: Us ambassador to india, sergio gor, arrived in ladakh thursday on his maiden visit to the union territory. India on Wednesday called for greater transparency and objectivity in UN Security Council sanctions decisions, saying membership of the powerful 15-nation body must not be used to “legitimise” terrorists, in a veiled criticism of Pakistan's role in dealing with terrorism Speaking at an open debate on the Council’s working methods on Wednesday, India’s Chargé d’Affaires at the UN, Ambassador Yojna Patel, said membership of the Security Council “must not become a platform to pursue narrow political interests”.“Presence in the Security Council must not be instrumentalised to legitimise terrorists by attempting to de-list them or to list other entities as terrorist organisations based solely on political considerations, without any objective criteria or supporting documentation,” she said, as quoted by ANI.India has long criticised the lack of transparency around proposals to designate terrorists and terror organisations. While approved listings are made public, New Delhi has pointed out that the reasons why proposals are rejected or placed under technical hold are not disclosed.India has previously described this practice as a “disguised veto” and has particularly criticised the functioning of the 1267 Al-Qaida Sanctions Committee.New Delhi has also faced resistance to attempts to designate Pakistan-based terrorists, with China, a permanent Council member, blocking or placing holds on some proposals.The Indian diplomat also raised concerns over the delayed appointment of chairs and vice-chairs of the Council’s subsidiary bodies. Eight months into 2026, several posts, including those overseeing the 1267 Al-Qaida and Taliban sanctions committees, remain unfilled.She called for a “definitive and non-negotiable” timeline to complete the appointments, saying the delay has affected the functioning of the subsidiary bodies.Denmark, which holds the Council presidency in August, described the delay as “unprecedented” and said it undermines the body’s effectiveness, credibility and institutional integrity.India also called for greater involvement of elected, non-permanent Council members in key processes, including the selection of the UN Secretary-General.Patel argued that the Council’s structure and working methods need to reflect the changes in the international system since 1945, when the UN was established. UN membership has since grown four-fold, she noted.“The world of 1945 has changed beyond recognition,” Patel said. “The outcome of one conflict 80 years ago cannot determine the composition, dynamics, approaches and working methods for perpetuity. This needs to change and must happen at the earliest.”
Article Summary: India has long criticised the lack of transparency around proposals to designate terrorists and terror organisations. The indian diplomat also raised concerns over the delayed appointment of chairs and vice-chairs of the council’s subsidiary bodies. She called for a “definitive and non-negotiable” timeline to complete the appointments.

Article Title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan moved to private hospital from prison after SC order
Article Text:

Imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan was shifted from Adiala prison to a private hospital in Islamabad after midnight Thursday for a medical examination, news agency AP reported citing Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party's statement.Khan was taken to Shifa International Hospital hours after Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the government would comply with a Supreme Court order directing authorities to facilitate his medical examination.The PTI said the transfer was carried out following the Supreme Court's order earlier this week but did not provide further details. It remained unclear whether Khan would return to prison after the examination or stay at the hospital for further treatment. His family and party have sought permission for him to remain there.Earlier Thursday, Chaudhry said the government had approached the Supreme Court seeking clarification on whether the medical relief granted to Khan applied only to him or could also cover other prisoners. He stressed that the request was not aimed at delaying or defying the court's order.The three-judge Supreme Court panel had ordered authorities two days earlier to take Khan to Shifa International Hospital for a medical examination amid prolonged concerns raised by his family and personal doctors over his health and access to treatment.The court directed that a medical board examine him, including specialists and his personal physician, Faisal Sultan.The government has maintained that prisoners receive medical care under existing rules and can be moved to government hospitals when required.Concerns over Khan's health intensified in January after his family claimed he had lost about 85% of the vision in his right eye. The government disputed the claim and later said his vision had improved by around 70%.Khan, a former cricket star, was ousted as prime minister in a parliamentary no-confidence vote in April 2022. He has remained imprisoned since 2023 after convictions in multiple cases, including a graft case.

Article Title: India, Japan deepen defence ties with maritime security pact; China challenge looms over Indo-Pacific
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 20 (ANI): Japan's Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi inspects the tri-services Guard of Honour at Manekshaw Centre, in New Delhi on Thursday. (ANI Photo/Naveen Sharma)

Rajnath Singh Announces Rs 8.75 Lakh Crore Defence Modernisation Push on 80th Independence Day

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and his Japanese counterpart Shinjirō Koizumi held a bilateral dialogue in New Delhi. Koizumi is on his maiden visit to India and the visit is seen as an expansion of the 'Special Strategic and Global Partnership' between the two countries, which is gaining importance in light of an assertive China across the Indo-Pacific region. The special strategic partnership, which was formalised in 2014 has continuously been strengthened by the leadership of the two countries, with PM Modi visiting Japan eight times. The strategic relationship has been anchored by shared democratic values and a common vision for a free and open Indo‑Pacific. During the meeting the defence minister of both the nations signed a Memorandum of Arrangement (MoA) on maritime security cooperation. This agreement provides a framework for strengthening cooperation between the naval forces of the two countries information sharing in the realm of maritime domain awareness and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR).Defence cooperation between New Delhi and Tokyo has accelerated in recent years. A series of agreements since 2014 have institutionalised exchanges, ranging from the Memorandum of Defence Cooperation to the Reciprocal Provision of Supplies and Services pact signed in 2020.This framework has been operationalised during naval wargames such as MILAN and JAIMEX. These exercises have enabled seamless logistics during visit of ships and aircraft alike. The co‑development of Japan's UNICORN integrated communications antenna system for the Indian Navy, a deal that was formalised in 2024, represents the first joint equipment project between the two countries.The current visit has seen the defence ministers of both nations reaffirm their commitment to maritime security cooperation, mine countermeasures and joint shipbuilding. Japan’s technological expertise and India’s production capabilities are being aligned under the “Make in India” framework, with discussions on reciprocal ship repair facilities progressing. The two sides welcomed the expansion of bilateral exercises, including Dharma Guardian and JAIMEX, and looked ahead to Veer Guardian 26, which will see Japanese fighter aircraft participate in India for the first time. Both ministers also emphasised the importance of deepening defence R&D cooperation between Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and Japan’s Acquisition Technology and Logistics Agency (ATLA), and confirmed plans to convene a Defence Industry Forum.The two countries have also decided to accelerate discussions towards convening the Fourth Japan-India foreign and defence ministerial (2+2) meeting that is scheduled to be held in Tokyo later this year. Besides this, Singh and Koizumi are working to further promote cooperation through the Indo-Pacific Logistics Network (IPLN). This initiative supports partner countries during natural disasters by facilitating the transportation of personnel and supplies for humaitarian assistance and disaster relief operations.Beyond defence, the visit reaffirmed the salience of economic security as a foundational pillar of the partnership. The synergy between Japan’s Free and Open Indo‑Pacific vision and India’s Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions (MAHASAGAR) initiative provides strategic impetus to cooperation. Both sides are committed to elevating economic security ties, recognising that prosperity and security are intertwined.The Japanese Defence Minister’s presence in India is thus more than ceremonial. It reflects a partnership that has evolved from cultural affinity into strategic convergence. The two nations have an enduring and rich cultural history, with links dating back to 752 AD, when Bodhisena, an Indian monk, consecrated the Great Buddha at Nara’s Todaiji Temple. In modern times, figures such as Swami Vivekananda, Rabindranath Tagore, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose and Rash Behari Bose deepened the bonds of friendship. The Japan‑India Association, founded in 1903, is Japan’s oldest international friendship body. From Bodhisena’s consecration at Nara to joint naval drills in the Indian Ocean, the arc of India‑Japan relations is long, resilient and central pillar to keeping the Indo-Pacific open for all.
Article Summary: Shinjirō koizumi is on his maiden visit to india and the visit is seen as an expansion of the 'special strategic and global partnership' between the two countries. The special strategic partnership, which was formalised in 2014, has continuously been strengthened by the leadership of both countries.

Article Title: "I'm grateful for every lesson": Gisele Bündchen’s candid Tom Brady divorce admission revealed the pain behind her new beginning

Gisele Bündchen opens up about Tom Brady divorce

Gisele Bündchen’s divorce from Tom Brady is no longer breaking news, but a deeply emotional 2024 interview still offers a revealing look at what the supermodel went through after their marriage ended. During a conversation with ABC News’ Robin Roberts, Bündchen struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage, her children and the new chapter she was trying to build.The interview, released in March 2024 as part of “IMPACT x Nightline: Gisele Bündchen: Climbing the Mountain,” came more than a year after Bündchen and Brady finalized their divorce in October 2022.Their split ended a relationship that had lasted 16 years and a marriage that had lasted 13. By the time Bündchen sat down with Roberts, however, she was trying to understand the experience as part of a larger personal transition rather than simply an ending.Roberts reminded her that she had previously described the divorce as “the death of a dream.” The comment immediately struck an emotional chord.“Well, when you say ...” the model began, before pausing and getting teary. “Sorry, guys, I didn't know ... can I have a little moment?”After collecting herself, Bündchen spoke about accepting a future she had never expected to have.“It's definitely a time of, you know, a transition that had to take place, and it's not something that you — I don't think you wish for that, you know?” she said. “But I think sometimes in life things happen. I feel so blessed because, like, I wouldn't change anything in my life. I had incredible experiences. I learned so much. I have my children, which are the biggest blessings in my life.“And now I get to create — it's a new season, a new chapter in my life, and I get to learn new things, and I get to walk my path in a different way, you know?“And I'm grateful for all of it. I'm grateful for every lesson.”Her words showed that the divorce was not something she viewed in simple terms. There was pain, but there was also gratitude for the years she shared with Brady and the family they created.Bündchen and Brady share two children, Benjamin and Vivian. Brady also has a son, Jack, with actress Bridget Moynahan. For Bündchen, co-parenting meant accepting that the children would grow up moving between two different households and sets of rules.“There's easier days than others. But it's amazing that the kids — they're super smart children,” Bündchen said, laughing. “They know what they can get away with. So I think it's natural that it has different rules, and kids just adapt and they're going to try to do what they want. And I can only control what I do.”She also emphasized the value of her children having relationships with both parents.“It's amazing that they get to spend time with both parents because it's more enriching for their lives, two different worlds, and they get to learn from two different worlds.”Bündchen spoke warmly about Brady’s oldest son, Jack, whom she helped raise during her years with the former NFL star.“I raised him. I love him,” she said.Looking ahead, Bündchen said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.“I'm very committed to living my truth more than ever, so I would say that's where my heart is now, where I am right now. I'm living my truth and I'm not apologizing for it,” she explained.The 2024 interview remains significant because it captured Bündchen at a vulnerable point in her life. She was not simply discussing a famous divorce. She was describing the difficult process of accepting change, protecting her children and finding an identity beyond a marriage that had once shaped so much of her public life.
Article Summary: Gisele bündchen and tom brady finalized their divorce in october 2022. The supermodel struggled to hold back tears while reflecting on the end of a 13-year marriage. She said she wanted to live according to her own values rather than public expectations.

A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. Article Title: Quote of the day by King Charles: "To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear…" - a tribute to Queen Elizabeth, on gratitude, service and a son's farewell
Article Text:
Quote of the day by King Charles (AP photo)

Quote of the day by King Charles

"To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late Papa, I want simply to say this: Thank you. Thank you for your love and devotion to our family and to the family of nations you have served so diligently all these years. May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest"

What is the meaning of King Charles' quote

Why King Charles thanked Queen Elizabeth II

The personal meaning behind "my darling Mama"

What "the family of nations" actually means

Why Charles' farewell centred on service

The Shakespeare reference at the end of the speech

How the quote reflects the relationship between duty and family

How to apply the message in daily life

Some other memorable quotes by King Charles

"I am a dangerous person because I mind about things."

"It is important to be able to stand back and see the bigger picture."

"The environment is something that is very close to my heart."

"I think we have to be very careful about what we do to the natural world."

Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son, King Charles III, addressed the nation the following day, speaking as both a new monarch and a grieving son at the same time. Recorded in the Blue Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace, with a framed portrait of his mother resting on the desk beside him, his tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service. It became one of the most widely remembered moments of that entire period, quoted on front pages across the country the following morning. For millions watching, the address offered a rare glimpse behind the crown, where duty and private grief briefly occupied space. His carefully chosen words also captured the enormous responsibility that had suddenly passed to him, making the moment deeply personal and historically significant.The speech also reassured a grieving public that the values associated with Elizabeth’s reign would continue, while Charles acknowledged the changes that lay ahead. His measured tone reflected both continuity and transition as Britain entered a new chapter.The address also marked the beginning of a new constitutional era, as Charles formally assumed the role his mother had held for seven decades. His message balanced continuity with change, reassuring the public while acknowledging the profound personal loss.At its heart, the message is about gratitude, love and farewell. Charles begins by describing his mother's death as a "last great journey," a gentle way of naming the end of a life, before referring directly to her reunion with her late husband, Prince Philip, who had died in April 2021. Rather than dwelling on the enormous constitutional change actually taking place, Charles places his mother's role firmly within a family context first. He thanks her for the love and devotion she gave to her family, before widening that same gratitude to the people and nations she served. The simplicity of the words "thank you," repeated before he expands on what he is actually grateful for, turns the tribute into an expression of appreciation for an entire lifetime of service.Queen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952 and remained on the throne for more than seven decades, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Across that period, she served under fifteen British prime ministers and witnessed enormous political, social and technological change. For Charles, though, her significance was never limited to her constitutional role alone. She was also, simply, his mother. His tribute moves between these two identities throughout, recognising her commitment to the "family of nations" she served while speaking about her in the deeply personal language of a son saying goodbye to his parent.The phrase "my darling Mama" gave the speech a genuinely intimate quality that stood apart from the formal language normally associated with royal addresses. Charles was speaking to a global audience, and yet the words themselves were directed towards one single person. Calling his mother "Mama" reflected the private family relationship sitting behind the public institution. Elizabeth II had been Queen to millions of people, but to her son she remained, simply, his mother. That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.Charles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.A central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.Charles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.One of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. In the same speech, he also announced that Prince William and Catherine would become the new Prince and Princess of Wales, and expressed his love for Harry and Meghan "as they continue to build their lives overseas," a reminder that even a historic constitutional address remained, underneath it, a message about family.The circumstances behind this quote are genuinely unique, but its central message of gratitude applies just as well to ordinary relationships. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.
Article Summary: Quote of the day by king charles: "to my darling mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late papa" queen elizabeth ii died on 8 september 2022, her eldest son, king charles iii, addressed the nation the following day. His tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service.
